questions.prompt: You make 38 into 40 by adding two pretend stickers. What must you do at the end?
questions.explanation: The two extra stickers were only there to make the sum easier. Remove them to get the real total.

questions.prompt: You meant to give away 29 stickers, but counted out 30. How do you fix it?
questions.explanation: You took away one more sticker than you meant to. Putting one back fixes the count.

questions.prompt: For 19 + 6, you first work out 20 + 6 = 26. What is the real answer?
questions.explanation: You added one pretend counter when you changed 19 to 20. Take it away from 26: the answer is 25.

title: Mental maths: round a number, then undo the change
practice: Try a round at your own pace. Use the examples above when you need a starting point.

sections.title: How does rounding help mental maths?
sections.html:
Use a nearby easy number, then undo the change to get the exact answer. For 38 + 27, try 40 + 27 = 67. You added two extra, so take them away: 65.

Think of the extra two as borrowed stickers. They made counting easier, but they cannot stay in your collection.

sections.title: Follow the two extra stickers
sections.html:
1. Make 38 into 40. Pretend you have two extra stickers.
  2. Add 27. Forty plus twenty is sixty; seven more makes 67.
  3. Remove the pretend extras. 67 − 2 = 65.

You could also move two from the 27 to the 38: 40 + 25 = 65. That is making a ten by moving, rather than adding, counters.

sections.title: What changes when you subtract?
sections.html:
For 72 − 29, take away 30 first: 72 − 30 = 42. You removed one too many, so put it back: 42 + 1 = 43.

In the addition example, remove the extra you added. Here, return the extra you took away.

sections.title: Try 19 + 6
sections.html:
Make 19 into 20, then add six. What should happen to the extra one?

Show the answer

20 + 6 = 26. Remove the one pretend counter: 25.

Draw dots or use objects if it helps. The last adjustment matters more than speed.

sections.title: Ask: what did I change?
sections.html:
Rounding gives you a convenient starting point, not permission to forget the difference. Undoing the change makes these answers exact.

OpenStax explains regrouping sums. For another shortcut, try multiplying by 11.

description: Make 38 + 27 easier by using 40, then take the extra two away. Try rounding and adjusting for addition and subtraction, with two short examples.
